title: fix(media): avoid blocking cold task lookups
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Cold media status, prompt, and duplicate lookups could block on configuration state when a restored task lacked a recorded requester, or lose that task while preparing requester facts.

## User Impact

Restored media tasks remain visible to their requester, completed or failed tasks produce the correct duplicate decision, and requester preparation uses the existing asynchronous config owner. A configuration-source change during the lookup rejects the interrupted lookup instead of returning missing or stale requester facts. Ordinary same-source config reloads preserve the captured snapshot. No schema, retention, provider, permission, or update migration changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

One preparation serves all enabled media prompt sections. Recorded identities and agent-scoped session keys avoid config loading; terminal-only status and prompt reads do too. After config preparation succeeds or fails, the lookup refreshes task rows and rechecks the captured owners before selection. The shared config reader exposes its existing source-currentness check so callers can retain it across subsequent awaits without duplicating selector policy.

## Evidence

Candidate `f955720b752c94d9c9966ac004944286c86ab093` carries the media repair onto main commit `829a681991220bcc2ec63ff5d7eebac8d3e2eea0`. All 69 focused tests across five files, 32 selected changed-file requirements, fresh independent P0–P2 review, and the normal full `pnpm build` passed. Two real-reader source-change regressions failed on the prior implementation and passed after repair; the same-source reload control passed in both cases. The original cold shared-prompt negative control remains retained at its original source identity.

Fresh compiled Node 24.21.0 and Bun 1.4.2 processes passed five scenarios each: terminal-only config avoidance, cold requester/prompt/duplicate lookup, persisted success, persisted failure, and reopen. Construction, close, six SQLite query methods, and `Atomics.wait` were positively calibrated and stayed zero during every measured phase and final cleanup. Feature-import counts were also zero. Canonical artifact ownership and matching before/after inventories bound 47,429 source entries, 14,015 artifacts, installation metadata, package manifests, and maintained links. Transitive dependency payload bytes were not exhaustively inventoried. Native fixture writes and SQLite capability/library selection are setup, outside the measured read interval; no external provider, updater, full Gateway, held-lock, fault-injection, or speedup claim is made.

The historical Doctor-path failure in [CI run 35533014346](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35533014346/job/106137117690) remains unexplained. This successor addresses the demonstrated config-source races and does not claim to repair that earlier failure. Fresh exact-head CI and native maintainer gates remain required before landing.

### Per-file test cost

Measured at the unchanged `f955720b752c94d9c9966ac004944286c86ab093` candidate on macOS arm64, Node 24.21.0, pnpm 12.4.0. Each file ran once, serially, using `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`; external wall time includes the full command and its normal preparation.

| Test file | Cases | External wall | Vitest invocation | Case execution total |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `src/agents/media-generation-task-status.cold.test.ts` | 4 passed | 101.91 s | 92.07 s | 9.311 s |
| `src/agents/media-generation-task-status-shared.test.ts` | 32 passed | 3.35 s | 1.86 s | 0.133 s |

The cold suite needs the real persisted task/config/worker boundary to prove requester selection, config-source rejection, and absence of parent-thread SQLite calls through cleanup. A mocked reader cannot establish that contract; the shared suite provides the cheaper decision/race coverage. This cold run had a normal compiled-worker cache miss: automatic worker preparation took 57.61 s, and Vitest attributed 84% of its invocation to transformation. All 47,429 tracked source entries matched before and after each command. The status test file only added a three-line owner mock, so its unchanged cases did not receive an additional cost run.

CI per-file timing is separate: it has not been extracted from the current CI run [35633562286](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35633562286). The measurements above are local command timings, not inferred CI file costs or whole-job durations.

The successful exact-head CI workflow took **1,617 seconds (26 minutes 57 seconds)** from creation at 17:40:59 UTC to completion at 18:07:56 UTC on September 21, 2026. The final `openclaw/ci-gate` job completed at that same timestamp. This is total workflow elapsed time, including queueing, setup, and parallel jobs; it is not a per-file test measurement.
